purpose: Build-time C-to-Bristol reference compiler for the private output-encryption relation. Not a replacement MPC engine, proof system or TLS library.

patch_scope: Preserve four Bison-generated .hpp headers when also supplying the legacy .h names. No parser grammar or circuit algorithm change.

build_flags: CXX='g++ -include limits -include memory -DCATCH_CONFIG_NO_POSIX_SIGNALS' CPP='g++ -include limits -include memory'
build_flag_scope: Supply missing standard-library declarations on the modern C++ toolchain; disable only Catch's alternate-signal-stack test crash handler for current glibc compatibility. No algorithm or compiler assertion is disabled.

additional_patches.scope: Expose the existing CBMC object-bits setting in the HyCC CLI, copying the option registration from the same pinned CBMC src/cbmc/cbmc_parse_options.h. No pointer-model implementation change.

Invoke the existing upstream CBMC rewrite_union pass immediately after remove_complex, matching the same pinned CBMC src/cbmc/cbmc_parse_options.cpp. The pass implementation and the cryptographic C libraries are unchanged.

Execute CBMC's generated C initializer and the compiled function in the same symbolic state. The upstream separate initialization state left static constants at unbound global#0 in the new stepper. No global becomes a public input and no cryptographic expression is replaced.
additional_patches.verification: The preceding cbmc-gc-unions compiler fails this exact constant-table/module regression with Unknown literal: 1. The patched compiler generates and merges the circuit; upstream circuit-utils --create-verifier plus CBMC proves equivalence to the C reference for all two uint32 inputs: VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL, 0 of 1 failed. Initial verifier attempt lacked the upstream required InputA/InputB/Output aliases and failed parsing before verification; corrected source supplied these aliases.

status: Full build and constant-initialization regression completed. Actual encryption compilation is ongoing; no generated ML-KEM or recipient-encryption circuit is yet accepted or claimed.
